discovery: Room-temperature tunnel magnetoresistance in magnetic tunnel junctions, including giant TMR with crystalline MgO barriers

nominees.name: Stuart S. P. Parkin
nominees.affiliation: Max Planck Institute of Microstructure Physics, Halle, Germany

motivation: In 1995 Miyazaki and, independently, Moodera showed large tunnel magnetoresistance at room temperature in ferromagnet/insulator/ferromagnet junctions. This turned spin-dependent tunnelling, which had been a low-temperature curiosity, into a usable physical effect. Parkin then showed giant TMR through coherent tunnelling in crystalline MgO barriers (2004), which raised the effect to hundreds of percent. The magnetic tunnel junction that resulted is the central element of spintronics. It replaced GMR sensors in hard-disk read heads, enabling the data explosion of the past two decades, and it is the storage cell of non-volatile MRAM now made in leading semiconductor foundries. The effect shows how quantum spin physics in nanostructures becomes a working technology that saves energy. Since the 2007 prize for GMR, TMR has become the more consequential descendant, and its discoverers deserve recognition.
